ask: C11, POSIX. logread.c: memory-mapped log scanner. mmap a file, iterate length-prefixed binary records (u32 len + body) without reading the whole file, validate bounds, count by severity byte, print the last N records of a requested severity, and unmap cleanly on every exit path. write the file.
prose:
`logread.c` is written. A few notes on the design:

**Record layout assumed**
```
[ u32 len ][ u8 severity | u8... text ]
```
The severity byte is the first byte of the body. Text payload follows it. A body of exactly 1 byte is valid (severity only, empty message).

**Two-pass index approach** — first pass walks the mapping once, bounds-checking every record and building a flat `Record[]`. The second pass filters by severity and prints the tail. This avoids rescanning for the tail and keeps the hot path off the mapping after the index is built.

**Bounds safety** — every field is range-checked before dereferencing. A truncated file or corrupt length field stops the scan early with a diagnostic rather than a segfault or silent wrap.

**Cleanup** — `MapCtx` holds fd + map so every early return goes through `cleanup()`. The fd is closed immediately after a successful `mmap` since the mapping keeps the data live independently.

**Build and run**
```sh
cc -std=c11 -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L -Wall -Wextra -o logread logread.c
./logread mylog.bin 3 20   # last 20 ERROR records
```

If you want to test it without an existing binary log, I can write a small `loggen.c` that emits random length-prefixed records with mixed severities.
